issues.t: Transmission slips or gets stuck in second gear
issues.sym: The truck won't shift past second gear, feels sluggish, revs high at highway speed, or slips between gears, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: The automatic can drop into a protective 'limp' mode that holds second gear. RepairPal has dozens of Raider reports, and updated engine/transmission computer software often helps. Mitsubishi also issued a 2007 bulletin for drivability problems fixed by reprogramming.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition, then have codes read. Ask a dealer about the computer software update before agreeing to a rebuild. Avoid long or heavy towing until it is fixed.

issues.t: Misfire and lost power from a dropped valve seat
issues.sym: A sudden misfire on one cylinder, rough running, a flashing check engine light, and noticeably less power.
issues.why: On the 3.7L V6 and 4.7L V8, a valve seat pressed into the cylinder head can loosen and fall out, usually after the engine has run hot. The valve can then no longer seal, and the cylinder loses compression.
issues.next: If the check engine light flashes, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Ask for a compression or leak-down test. The fix is a rebuilt or replacement cylinder head.

issues.t: Head gasket failure after overheating
issues.sym: White exhaust smoke with a sweet smell, milky oil, coolant disappearing with no visible leak, or overheating.
issues.why: The 4.7L V8 does not tolerate overheating well, and a head gasket is a common casualty of a cooling system failure.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Have a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test done. Fixing the cooling problem that caused it is part of the repair.

issues.t: Coolant leaks and overheating
issues.sym: Coolant puddles or crust under the front of the truck, a low coolant tank, steam from under the hood, or a rising temperature gauge.
issues.why: The water pump, thermostat, radiator, fan and hoses on these V6 and V8 engines wear with age. Because both engines are hurt badly by overheating, small leaks matter.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold and watch the gauge. Pull over and shut off the engine if it runs hot. Have leaks fixed quickly to protect the cylinder heads.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the engine, a burning-oil smell, or light smoke from the engine bay after driving.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gaskets harden and crack with age, especially past 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly. Have both sides replaced at once; it is a moderate-cost repair and stops oil from dripping on hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Ticking noise and misfire from stuck lash adjusters
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the top of the engine, rough idle or misfire.
issues.why: The 3.7L V6 uses hydraulic lash adjusters that can stick when oil is old, sludgy or the wrong thickness.
issues.next: Use the correct oil and change it on time. If ticking comes with a misfire, have a shop pinpoint the cylinder; replacing the stuck adjuster is the fix.

issues.t: Rough idle and oil leaks from a clogged PCV valve
issues.sym: Rough idle, hesitation, worse fuel economy, and new oil leaks from seals or gaskets.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) valve on the 3.7L can gum up, which builds pressure inside the engine and helps form sludge.
issues.next: Replace the PCV valve; the part is cheap, though it can be hard to reach. Change the oil afterward.

issues.t: PCV system can freeze in extreme cold
issues.sym: In very cold weather, oil leaks, rough running, or oil pushed out of seals after cold starts.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a 2008 bulletin for the crankcase ventilation system freezing in extreme cold, which traps pressure in the engine.
issues.next: If you live in a very cold area, ask a dealer about the PCV bulletin and any updated parts.

issues.t: Shudder or harsh 1-2 and 2-3 shifts
issues.sym: A shudder like driving over rumble strips at light throttle, or hard shifts from first to second or second to third.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued 2007 and 2008 bulletins for torque converter clutch shudder and harsh upshifts on these trucks.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about the transmission bulletins. A fluid service or software update may fix it before the converter is damaged.

issues.t: Check engine light with code P2181
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P2181 (cooling system performance), often with no other symptoms.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a bulletin to reprogram the engine computer with new software for this code.
issues.next: Check that the coolant is full and the gauge reads normal. If so, ask a dealer about the software update; if not, have the cooling system checked first.

issues.t: Clunk or pop from the steering shaft
issues.sym: A clunk or popping felt through the steering wheel when turning, especially at low speed or parking.
issues.why: The intermediate steering shaft between the column and steering gear wears and binds. RepairPal has reports across all Raider years, often around 75,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the steering shaft and front steering parts inspected. Lubricating or replacing the shaft usually fixes it.

issues.t: Rear axle pinion nut can loosen and lock the axle
issues.sym: A clunk or whine from the rear axle, play in the driveshaft, or in the worst case the rear wheels locking at speed.
issues.why: On this rear axle, shared with the Dodge Dakota, the pinion nut can back off, letting the gears damage each other. An owner reports the axle locking up at highway speed at about 102,000 miles. The Raider has no recall for this.
issues.next: If you hear new rear-axle noise or feel driveline clunks, have the pinion nut and axle checked right away. Don't drive it if the axle grinds.

issues.t: ABS computer can lock rear brakes (recall)
issues.sym: The rear wheels lock up early during hard or certain braking, making the truck harder to control.
issues.why: The ABS control module may upset the front-to-rear brake balance. Recall 06V038000 has dealers replace the ABS module.
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to check your VIN for recall 06V038000. Brake gently and leave extra room until it is checked.

issues.t: Static shock can upset lights, signals and wipers (recall)
issues.sym: Turn signals, headlights or wipers stop working or act strangely without warning.
issues.why: Static electricity from the driver can upset the instrument cluster electronics. Recall 06V039000 has dealers re-flash the cluster.
issues.next: Ask a Mitsubishi dealer to check your VIN for recall 06V039000. Don't drive at night or in rain if the lights or wipers misbehave.

issues.t: Manual-transmission truck may start in gear (recall)
issues.sym: The engine starts without pressing the clutch, or the truck lurches when started.
issues.why: Return springs in the clutch interlock switch can break on 2006 manual-transmission trucks built July 2005 to July 2006. Recall 14V-795 replaces the switch.
issues.next: Always press the clutch and keep your foot on the brake when starting. Ask a dealer to check for recall 14V-795.

issues.t: Takata driver airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The driver's frontal airbag inflator can absorb moisture over time and rupture when it deploys, throwing metal fragments. Mitsubishi replaces it free, including bags already replaced once under an earlier recall.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls or with a Mitsubishi dealer and get it fixed as soon as possible. Owners report parts delays, so book early.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning signs before a crash.
issues.why: The passenger frontal airbag inflator can degrade and rupture when it deploys. The recall was expanded to cover 2006–2009 Raiders, and dealers replace the inflator free.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls. Until it is fixed, avoid having anyone ride in the front passenger seat if possible.

issues.t: Water leak onto the passenger floor
issues.sym: Wet carpet on the passenger side after rain or a car wash, especially if parked nose-up on a slope.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a 2010 bulletin for water getting past the cowl trim at the base of the windshield.
issues.next: Dry the carpet to prevent mold and electrical problems, then have the cowl area resealed.

issues.t: Water inside headlights or lamps
issues.sym: Fog or droplets inside a headlight or lamp that don't clear.
issues.why: A bulletin explains how to tell normal condensation from water getting in through a bad seal or damaged lamp.
issues.next: Light fog that clears when the lights are on is normal. Standing water needs a resealed or new lamp.

issues.t: Brake pedal shudder at highway speeds
issues.sym: Vibration in the brake pedal or steering wheel when braking from highway speed.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued a 2006 bulletin for brake shudder on these trucks, usually from uneven rotor wear.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and replaced or resurfaced, and make sure wheel lug nuts are tightened evenly.

issues.t: No crank, no start and no dash lights
issues.sym: Turning the key does nothing, and the dash lights stay dark, even with a good battery.
issues.why: Mitsubishi issued bulletins for no-crank conditions caused by lost communication with the front control module.
issues.next: Check battery connections first. If they are good, have a shop check the front control module and its wiring.

issues.t: Speedometer stops working in cold weather
issues.sym: The speedometer needle drops to zero or won't move in cold temperatures.
issues.why: A Mitsubishi bulletin covers an inoperative speedometer in cold weather on this truck.
issues.next: Use a GPS app for speed until it is fixed, and ask a dealer about the bulletin.
